headline: High: Semantic Kernel can write and call MCP/API tools while awesome-nlp is a non-runnable docs-only list, so the main risks are B-side leakage and downstream action misuse rather than direct pair interaction.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-nlp is a non-runnable awesome-list with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot ingest Semantic Kernel outputs by default. Semantic Kernel can use MCP and plugins, but without a shared channel or a runnable target in agent_a, the prompt-injection pathway is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF agent_a is wrapped in a separate runtime that reads Semantic Kernel outputs automatically, the pathway changes.
IF a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge is added between the pair, injection becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep agent_a as a static reference artifact, not an executable consumer.
Do not connect agent_b MCP tools to any parser that treats agent_a text as instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags before any cross-agent handoff.
requires-engineering: isolate the pair with separate workspaces and no shared message bus.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Semantic Kernel reads files, writes files, and can call external APIs, so application context and secrets can leave the local boundary. awesome-nlp itself has no data surfaces, but if it is used as shared reference material in the same workspace, agent_b can expose that content through its broad egress. The pairwise leakage path is therefore one-sided and moderate.
conditions: IF agent_b is given files containing secrets or regulated data, those contents can be sent to external model providers or tools.
IF agent_a is placed in a shared workspace with sensitive notes, agent_b can read and exfiltrate them.
mitigations: Restrict agent_b to a redacted workspace.
Disable or proxy external API calls for sensitive runs.
Separate secrets from any files agent_b can read.
requires-engineering: add per-file allowlists for agent_b reads.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on outbound tool calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: There is no direct write-write conflict because awesome-nlp is not runnable and has no write surface. Semantic Kernel, however, can write files and use MCP tools, so if both are pointed at the same application-defined files or shared workspace, agent_b can overwrite or race with artifacts derived from agent_a. The conflict exists only through shared mutable resources.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to operate on the same writable directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF agent_b plugins mutate shared application state, concurrent updates can race.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Turn off write access for agent_b unless needed.
Serialize any shared-state updates through one operator.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared files or state.
requires-engineering: move shared artifacts to an append-only store.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Semantic Kernel is explicitly an orchestration layer that can pass model outputs into plugins and downstream actions, so it may treat upstream text as actionable. awesome-nlp is only a curated list, so it will not verify or correct those outputs. If agent_a-derived content is fed into agent_b workflows, errors can cascade into tool calls or generated responses.
conditions: IF agent_a content is copied into agent_b prompts or plugin inputs without verification, errors can propagate.
IF agent_b is allowed to act on generated facts, downstream mistakes can become operational.
mitigations: Require human review before agent_b acts on agent_a-derived claims.
Add a verification step for any facts imported from agent_a.
Limit agent_b to drafting, not executing, for high-stakes tasks.
requires-engineering: add citation checks before tool execution.
requires-engineering: separate retrieval from action-taking plugins.

E_compliance.rationale: Semantic Kernel can handle model provider API keys and plugin credentials and may send application context to Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Hugging Face, or MCP servers. awesome-nlp is a docs-only open-source list, so it does not itself create a residency issue, but the pair can still route regulated data through agent_b to third-party services. The compliance risk is therefore driven by agent_b alone.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into agent_b prompts or files, it may be transmitted to external providers.
IF deployment policy requires local-only processing, agent_b violates that policy when egress is enabled.
mitigations: Do not send regulated data to agent_b.
Use a local-only model provider for sensitive workloads.
Review plugin destinations before enabling them.
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing rules.
requires-engineering: implement retention and deletion controls for agent_b logs.
